title: The Unquiet Alibi
premise: Emrys Crane, the reclusive coroner of the tidal town of Marrow Bay, is approached by a nervous stranger who pays her to certify that no murder has occurred — a pre-emptive alibi for a killing he claims hasn't happened yet. When a body surfaces exactly as described, Emrys realizes the man is being framed by someone with access to the coroner's own files, and her long-cultivated invisibility makes her the only witness the law won't believe. Going outside official channels, she baits the killer by leaking a false autopsy detail, forcing a confrontation on the mudflats at low tide where the truth — and the town's buried complicity — finally gives itself up. In the end, justice arrives not through a courtroom but through the town's own reckoning, and Emrys accepts that belonging means letting herself be seen.
about_author: Ada Eriksen is the pen name of a former coastal records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed deaths along the northern seaboard. She writes mysteries about the people towns prefer to forget.

chapters.title: Paid in Full
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A stranger named Hollis Vane pays Emrys in cash to confirm, in advance, that no murder has occurred in Marrow Bay — and leaves behind a date. Emrys, who values her anonymity above all, is unsettled enough to quietly check the tide charts and morgue logs. The emotional beat is wary curiosity curdling into dread when she finds a file with her own signature that she never wrote.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, with a brief interlude from Deputy Sorrel Nkemelu's perspective. A body washes up matching Vane's description exactly; the planted file makes Vane the obvious suspect, and the town — which has always kept Emrys at arm's length — closes ranks against him. Sorrel notices the forged paperwork but is pressured to look away. The beat is isolation deepening: Emrys realizes her invisibility now protects a killer.

chapters.title: The Second Signature
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Working outside the law, she traces the forged file to someone with coroner's-office access and discovers a pattern of staged deaths covering the town's old smuggling debts — deaths she certified in good faith. She plants a false autopsy detail to flush the killer out. The beat is cold fury and resolve as Emrys, for the first time, chooses to be visible.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: Emrys and Sorrel's alternating POV. The killer takes the bait and comes for the false file, cornering Emrys on the exposed mudflats as the tide turns; Sorrel arrives not to arrest Emrys but to stand witness. The town's complicity is dragged into the open, and the killer is taken by the water he used so often. The beat is hard-won belonging: Emrys signs her real name to the true report, seen at last.
